 THIS CRIMINAL MISC. CASE HAVING COME UP FOR ADMISSION ON 06.11.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY PASSED THE FOLLOWING:
Rajesh vs State Of Kerala on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33658534/
1  Crl.MC.No. 8316 of 2025  2025:KER:85745  2  ORDER (Dated this the 06th day of November, 2025)

The petitioner is the sole accused in Crime No. 440 of 2025 of Cheranelloor Police Station involving offences under Section 376 of IPC, Section 126(2),
115(2) and 296(b) of BNS.

The prosecution case as revealed from the FIR is that the accused person after promising to marry the defacto complainant took her on 17.07.2021 to a flat at Kakkanad and had sexual intercourse with her by force.
Thereafter, when she came to know that the accused has relation with other ladies, she retracted from the relationship.

Due to that enmity, on 22.08.2025, at about 08.10 am, he caused hurt to the defacto complainant by slapping on her cheek, holding on her hair and kicked her head against the compound wall and thereby the alleged have committed the aforesaid offences.

2. According to the learned Counsel for the petitioner, the allegations against the petitioner does not constitute the offence under Section 376 IPC and further according to him, now the matter has been settled with the defacto complainant.
Therefore, he prayed for quashing the 2025:KER:85745 proceedings against the petitioner.
The learned Counsel for the petitioner also relyed upon the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Amol Bhagawan Nehul v. State of Maharashtra[2025 KHC 6552].

entities.text: Amol Bhagawan Nehul v. State of Maharashtra[2025 KHC 6552]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the above decision in para.9, the Appex Court held that "In our considered view, this is also not a case where there was a false promise to marry to begin with.
A consensual relationship turning sour or partners becoming distant
cannot be a ground for invoking criminal machinery of the State.
Such conduct not only burdens the Courts, but blots the identity of an individual accused of such a heinous offence.

This Court has time and again warned against the misuse of the provisions, and has termed it a folly(Naim Ahmed v. State (NCT) of Delhi, 2023 SCC OnLine SC 89)
to treat each breach of promise to marry as a false promise and prosecute a person for an offence under S. 376 IPC."
3.
The petition was opposed by the learned Public Prosecutor.
4. The defacto complainant filed affidavit stating that she had settled the dispute with the petitioner and also that she does not want to proceed with the case.
The learned Public Prosecutor upon instructions submitted that she had given signed statement to the SHO in tune with the 2025:KER:85745 affidavit filed in this case.
5. Even as per the FI Statement, the defacto complainant was already married and her marriage was in subsistence when she had made friendship with the petitioner.

It is true that in the FI Statement,
she stated that she came to know about the fact that the petitioner was married only subsequent to the alleged incident.

However, from the FI statement it is clear that, it was the defacto complainant who retracted from the relationship, because, on enquiry she found that the petitioner had relationship with other ladies.

Being aggrieved by the above conduct of the defacto complainant, the Rajesh vs State Of Kerala on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/33658534/
2 petitioner again approached her and assaulted her on 22.08.2025.
Since at the time of the alleged offence, the defacto complainant was married, the contention that she had consented to the relationship on the basis of the promise of marriage cannot be believed.
Therefore, the relationship between the petitioner and the defacto complainant is to be considered as a consensual one.
Moreover, the defacto complainant has now settled the dispute with the petitioner.
In the above circumstances, further proceedings against the petitioner will only be an abuse of the process of the court 2025:KER:85745 and as such it is liable to be quashed.
In the result, this Crl.MC is allowed.
